newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mixed on moderate volumes.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mixed on moderate volumes.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended little changed Thursday, as the complex continued to consolidate following last month's slide, but volumes were good for a low volatility day, traders said.

"There's support in spot gold around $368-369, but it may take a further decline of a few hundred points in the Dow Jones Index to lift gold prices much higher," said Jeff Singer, chief bullion trader at Imperial Bank in California.
"In the meantime, a lot of people are happy being short, with holiday jewelry demand over now and demand down in the rest of the world because of the dollar's strength," he said.
COMEX February gold ended up 20 cents at $370.80 an ounce, after trading in a $369.70-371.10 range on estimated total volume near the close of 31,000 lots.
Spot gold in the bullion market ended quoted $368.90/369.40, up from the London Thursday afternoon fix at $368.60, and the New York close Wednesday at $368.60/369.10.
COMEX March silver ended unchanged at $4.860 an ounce, after trading in a narrow $4.835-4.890 range on estimated total volumes near the close of 11,000 lots.
"While gold prices may sell off further, there are indications that $364 represents a solid base," CPM Group analyst Edward Kempf said.
"There have been signs of significant buying in Asia when gold trades below $370," he said.
Precious metals have been consolidating in the past 10 days after spot gold slid to a three year low at $366.00 an ounce at the end of November.

The complex has also received some support from volatility in stock and bond markets in the past week, but both the U.S. debt and equity markets steadied Thursday, helped by a benign November CPI report and weak November retail sales.
NYMEX January platinum ended down $1.30 at $371.00 an ounce, while NYMEX March palladium closed down $1.35 at $119.00.
Platinum remained the weakest contract in the complex, though there was good interest in buying the April platinum/April gold spread now it had narrowed back to near zero again, traders said.
The April platinum/gold spread slipped to 50 cents an ounce Thursday from $1.70 Wednesday, continuing its decline from a two month high at $9.40 on November 21.
News of problems in the annual contract negotiations between the Russians and Japanese over 1997 contract sales of platinum was causing nervousness in the platinum group metals markets, traders said.
--Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk,+1-212-859-1641; email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
